raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What does this PR do?

### Why This Contract Changes

Previously, Mamba preparation returned `(branch_input, residual, connection_state, replay_context)`:
- Ordinary Mamba used residual
- Wide Residual used `connection_state`, which already contained the residual. 


This PR introduces `ResidualBranchInput(branch_input, state):`
- `branch_input` is the activation prepared for the mixer, including normalization and dtype handling.
- `state` contains whatever the matching residual update needs:
  -Ordinary Mamba stores its residual tensor
  -Current WR stores (wide_residual,).

- The shared forward runs the mixer on `branch_input` and passes `state` unchanged to the layer’s update hook. 


Each implementation owns the state’s structure and meaning.
This provides a small integration point for future token-dependent Wide-Residual or mHC implementations: preparation can save predicted coefficients or mixing/write maps, and the matching update can consume them without changing the shared mixer execution.

**This PR adapts ordinary Mamba and WR only; mHC integration remains follow-up work.**
 
  
 ### Summary

This refactor introduces `ResidualBranchInput(branch_input, state)`: the shared forward executes the branch and passes its saved state unchanged to the implementation-specific residual-update hook.

- Ordinary Mamba saves its residual tensor.
- Current WR saves `(wide_residual,)`.
- Each implementation controls preparation, normalization, precision, and writeback.
- A packaging hook preserves the existing two-stage interfaces used by ShortcutMoE.

Residual mathematics, parameter ownership, and replay policy are preserved.

## Refactoring Plan

Stage 2A of #7888, following the replay-planning refactor in #7923.

This establishes a small common contract through ordinary and WR Mamba.
Future token-dependent WR variants or mHC adapters can save additional
coefficients needed at writeback while reusing the branch forward.
Their integration and cross-layer state transport remain subsequent work.

<!-- nemo-ci-review-impact:v1 ceiling=low -->

**Light review: Mamba branch execution now goes through `ResidualBranchInput`**

The refactor keeps behavior the same on every path I traced. I found no correctness, test-coverage, or documentation problems. There is one small style-guide nit, posted inline. It is annotation-only and does not block the PR.

What I checked against base:
- **WR two-stage tuple:** [`WideResidualMambaLayer._pack_two_stage_output`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f5de30a9324ce876172dbe7446c1399fb3468807/megatron/core/ssm/wide_residual_mamba_layer.py#L151-L156) returns `write_state[0]`. Base returned `self.residual_read.residual_stream(connection_state)` instead. These give the same tensor: [`ResidualConnection.residual_stream`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f5de30a9324ce876172dbe7446c1399fb3468807/megatron/core/transformer/residual_connection.py#L231-L238) is a staticmethod that validates the state and returns `state[0]`, and `StreamwiseSigmoidWideResidualConnection` does not override it. The validation call still runs before normalization, so a hook-modified read is still rejected at the same point.
- **ShortcutMoE:** [`ShortcutMoEBlock.forward`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f5de30a9324ce876172dbe7446c1399fb3468807/megatron/core/models/hybrid/shortcut_block.py#L519-L564) still unpacks `*paired_state` into `forward_post_core_attn`. The tuples are unchanged: `(ssm_output, residual)` for ordinary Mamba and `(ssm_output, residual, connection_state)` for WR. WR's `forward_post_core_attn` now passes only `connection_state` to `_apply_mixer_update`. Base never used `residual` there anyway.
- **Replay policy:** unchanged. Ordinary Mamba returns `None` for the context. WR still checkpoints the read and a non-`IdentityOp` norm, and checkpoints the write only when it is not the block end.
- **Python version:** a generic `NamedTuple` needs Python 3.11 or later, and `pyproject.toml` requires `>=3.12`, so `ResidualBranchInput[ResidualConnectionState]` in the WR return annotation is safe.
- **Old private signatures:** I looked for callers of the old 4-tuple `_prepare_mixer_state` and the old `_apply_mixer_update(residual, connection_state)` in `test_residual_recompute.py`, `test_shortcut_block.py`, `test_hybrid_block.py` and `test_wide_shortcut_parallel.py`. None remain, and [`test_mamba_layer.py`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f5de30a9324ce876172dbe7446c1399fb3468807/tests/unit_tests/ssm/test_mamba_layer.py#L75-L189) was updated to the new binding.
- **New tests:** [`test_mamba_residual_state.py`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f5de30a9324ce876172dbe7446c1399fb3468807/tests/unit_tests/ssm/test_mamba_residual_state.py) compares the new forward against the old eager schedule. It checks outputs, gradients, the operator trace, the RNG state and hooks, and also covers two-stage parity, replay selection and legacy state-dict loading. The CPU path it relies on exists (`streamwise_residual_ops` has a pure-PyTorch fallback), and the `SimpleNamespace` config has every field the WR connection constructors read. I reasoned through these tests but did not run them.

nodes.body:
btw, I think the two-stage path only half follows the new contract. `forward_pre_attn_and_core_attn` now goes through `_prepare_mixer_state` + `_pack_two_stage_output`, but base `forward_post_core_attn` still calls `_apply_mixer_bda(out, residual)` directly and skips `_apply_mixer_update`. So a subclass that only overrides prepare/update/pack (the extension story in the PR description) would quietly get the ordinary BDA on the ShortcutMoE path, or crash if `write_state` isn't a tensor.

Maybe just route it through the hook? For ordinary Mamba `write_state` is the residual, so behavior stays identical:
```python
return self._apply_mixer_update(mixer_out_with_bias, residual)
```
Might also be worth adding a two-stage case to `test_shared_schedule_keeps_state_opaque_and_call_local`, since right now it only covers single-stage `forward`.

+    StreamwiseSigmoidWideResidualConnection,
+    load_residual_state,

+class _Mixer(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, dtype) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.projection = nn.Linear(8, 8, dtype=dtype)
+
+    def forward_pre_attn_and_core_attn(self, value, **kwargs):
+        return value * 0.5
+
+    def forward_post_core_attn(self, value):
+        return self.projection(value), None
+
+    def forward(self, value, **kwargs):
+        return self.forward_post_core_attn(self.forward_pre_attn_and_core_attn(value))
+
+
+class _OperatorTrace(TorchDispatchMode):
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.calls = []
+
+    def __torch_dispatch__(self, function, types, args=(), kwargs=None):
+        self.calls.append(str(function))
+        return function(*args, **(kwargs or {}))
+
+
+def _layer(wide, fp32, dropout=0.0):
+    # Isolate the real layer schedule from GPU-only mixer construction. The registered
+    # norm, mixer and WR reader/writer remain real modules with real autograd execution.
+    cls = WideResidualMambaLayer if wide else MambaLayer
+    layer = cls.__new__(cls)
+    nn.Module.__init__(layer)
+    layer.config = SimpleNamespace(
+        hidden_size=8,
+        params_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        fp32_residual_connection=fp32,
+        bias_dropout_fusion=False,
+        sequence_parallel=False,
+        wide_residual=WideResidualConfig(num_streams=3, learned_retention=True) if wide else None,
+    )
+    layer.layer_number = 1
+    layer.hidden_dropout = dropout
+    layer.norm = nn.LayerNorm(8, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    layer.mixer = _Mixer(torch.bfloat16)
+    layer.mamba_bda = get_bias_dropout_add
+    layer.bias_dropout_add_exec_handler = torch.enable_grad
+    if wide:
+        layer.residual_read = StreamwiseSigmoidWideResidualConnection(
+            layer.config, 1, "mamba", operation="read"
+        )
+        layer.residual_write = StreamwiseSigmoidWideResidualConnection(
+            layer.config, 1, "mamba", operation="write"
+        )
+        layer.register_load_state_dict_pre_hook(load_residual_state)
+    return layer
+
+
+def _parent_forward(layer, value, wide):
+    """The eager schedule before opaque write-state plumbing (main d56953fb08)."""
+    if wide:
+        branch, state = layer.residual_read(
+            value,
+            fp32_residual_connection=layer.config.fp32_residual_connection,
+            branch_input_dtype=layer.config.params_dtype,
+        )
+        layer.residual_read.residual_stream(state)
+        branch = layer.norm(branch.to(layer.config.params_dtype))
+    else:
+        residual = layer._prepare_residual(value)
+        branch = layer._prepare_mixer_input(value)
+    output = layer.mixer(branch)
+    if wide:
+        with layer.bias_dropout_add_exec_handler():
+            return layer.residual_write(
+                output,
+                state=state,
+                dropout_probability=layer.hidden_dropout,
+                training=layer.training,
+            )
+    return layer._apply_mixer_bda(output, residual)
+

+    reference.train(mode == "train")

+    reference_events = []

+        for name in ("residual_read", "norm", "mixer", "residual_write"):

+    assert actual_trace.calls == expected_trace.calls

+    assert torch.equal(torch.get_rng_state(), expected_rng)
+    if mode in ("train", "eval"):

+def test_shared_schedule_keeps_state_opaque_and_call_local(monkeypatch, two_stage):
+    layer = _layer(False, False)
+    contexts = []
+    updates = []
+
+    def prepare(value, residual_stream_recompute_context=None):
+        # Neither a tensor nor a residual-first tuple: only the matching update knows it.
+        state = SimpleNamespace(residual=value)
+        contexts.append(state)
+        return ResidualBranchInput(value, state), None

+    def update(output, state, recompute_context=None):

+        first_stage = layer.forward_pre_attn_and_core_attn(
+            first, residual_stream_recompute_context=object()
+        )
+        second_stage = layer.forward_pre_attn_and_core_attn(
+            second, residual_stream_recompute_context=object()

+        layer.forward_post_core_attn(*second_stage)


This only adds annotations, so runtime and test behavior stay the same. To verify: every `def __init__` in this file should end in `-> None:`, and the test results should be unchanged.

btw, I think the two-stage path only half follows the new contract. `forward_pre_attn_and_core_attn` now goes through `_prepare_mixer_state` + `_pack_two_stage_output`, but base `forward_post_core_attn` still calls `_apply_mixer_bda(out, residual)` directly and skips `_apply_mixer_update`. So a subclass that only overrides prepare/update/pack (the extension story in the PR description) would quietly get the ordinary BDA on the ShortcutMoE path, or crash if `write_state` isn't a tensor.

Maybe just route it through the hook? For ordinary Mamba `write_state` is the residual, so behavior stays identical:

```python
return self._apply_mixer_update(mixer_out_with_bias, residual)
```

**Light review: Mamba branch execution now goes through `ResidualBranchInput`**

The refactor keeps behavior the same on every path I traced. I found no correctness, test-coverage, or documentation problems. There is one small style-guide nit, posted inline. It is annotation-only and does not block the PR.

What I checked against base:
- **WR two-stage tuple:** [`WideResidualMambaLayer._pack_two_stage_output`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f5de30a9324ce876172dbe7446c1399fb3468807/megatron/core/ssm/wide_residual_mamba_layer.py#L151-L156) returns `write_state[0]`. Base returned `self.residual_read.residual_stream(connection_state)` instead. These give the same tensor: [`ResidualConnection.residual_stream`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f5de30a9324ce876172dbe7446c1399fb3468807/megatron/core/transformer/residual_connection.py#L231-L238) is a staticmethod that validates the state and returns `state[0]`, and `StreamwiseSigmoidWideResidualConnection` does not override it. The validation call still runs before normalization, so a hook-modified read is still rejected at the same point.
- **ShortcutMoE:** [`ShortcutMoEBlock.forward`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f5de30a9324ce876172dbe7446c1399fb3468807/megatron/core/models/hybrid/shortcut_block.py#L519-L564) still unpacks `*paired_state` into `forward_post_core_attn`. The tuples are unchanged: `(ssm_output, residual)` for ordinary Mamba and `(ssm_output, residual, connection_state)` for WR. WR's `forward_post_core_attn` now passes only `connection_state` to `_apply_mixer_update`. Base never used `residual` there anyway.
- **Replay policy:** unchanged. Ordinary Mamba returns `None` for the context. WR still checkpoints the read and a non-`IdentityOp` norm, and checkpoints the write only when it is not the block end.
- **Python version:** a generic `NamedTuple` needs Python 3.11 or later, and `pyproject.toml` requires `>=3.12`, so `ResidualBranchInput[ResidualConnectionState]` in the WR return annotation is safe.
- **Old private signatures:** I looked for callers of the old 4-tuple `_prepare_mixer_state` and the old `_apply_mixer_update(residual, connection_state)` in `test_residual_recompute.py`, `test_shortcut_block.py`, `test_hybrid_block.py` and `test_wide_shortcut_parallel.py`. None remain, and [`test_mamba_layer.py`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f5de30a9324ce876172dbe7446c1399fb3468807/tests/unit_tests/ssm/test_mamba_layer.py#L75-L189) was updated to the new binding.
- **New tests:** [`test_mamba_residual_state.py`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f5de30a9324ce876172dbe7446c1399fb3468807/tests/unit_tests/ssm/test_mamba_residual_state.py) compares the new forward against the old eager schedule. It checks outputs, gradients, the operator trace, the RNG state and hooks, and also covers two-stage parity, replay selection and legacy state-dict loading. The CPU path it relies on exists (`streamwise_residual_ops` has a pure-PyTorch fallback), and the `SimpleNamespace` config has every field the WR connection constructors read. I reasoned through these tests but did not run them.
